stem: Meena's mother packs her lunchbox with rice, chapati, and a spoon of ghee. She tells Meena that these foods give her body energy to play and study. Why are carbohydrates and fats called energy-giving food components?

options.text: They protect the body from diseases.
They provide energy for performing activities.
They help the body grow and repair itself.
They keep the body cool in summer.

teacher.key_rationale: Carbohydrates (rice, chapati) and fats (ghee) supply energy for daily activities, so they are classified as energy-giving foods. Disease protection is the role of vitamins and minerals (A), growth and repair is the role of proteins (C), and cooling is not a classification function (D).
